description: ACL rule keys are a CLOSED set (PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.1, spec v1.27.0, #107). Loading a rule that carries any key outside `callers`, `targets`, `effect`, `approval`, `description`, `conditions` MUST fail with ACLRuleError. (`approval` joined the set in spec v1.28.0, §6.1.6; this fixture originally used it as its example of an unrecognised key, which stopped being true the moment #108 landed — an example must be chosen so that it cannot become valid later.) A key nothing evaluates is otherwise dropped in silence, which widens an `allow` rule with no warning — the §6.1.1 defect class on the pattern side. `id`, `actions` and `priority` were reserved in earlier revisions and are evaluated by no implementation; they are rejected like any other unknown key, and an implementation SHOULD name them as reserved. Driver contract: build an ACL FILE containing `rule` under `rules:` with the given `default_effect`, load it through the SDK's file-loading entry point, and assert that loading succeeds when `expected_load` is "ok" and raises/returns an ACL rule error when it is "reject". Where the SDK exposes the message, assert it names the offending key.

test_cases.note: Control: the closed set itself must still load.
Both optional members of the closed set.

THE ESCALATION CASE. An operator writing `actions: ["describe"]` intends introspection only; before v1.27.0 the key was dropped and the rule granted execute on orders.* to every agent.* caller, with no warning. Being a schema-DECLARED property is why `additionalProperties: false` could not catch it — it is removed from the schema in the same change.
Reserved; note the schema documented it as having no effect on rule ordering, which first-match-wins already fixes.

An invented key. Silently dropping it would degrade the rule to a bare `allow` — which is why closing the set is a prerequisite for adding any new rule field. NOTE: this case used `approval` until v1.28.0 made that key real; a "does not exist" example must be one that cannot later become valid.
`conditons` for `conditions`. Dropped silently before v1.27.0, so the rule granted unconditionally — the same shape as the misspelled-condition-key defect §6.1.2 closed, one level up.
A reserved key and an invented one together; the message should account for both rather than stopping at the first.
§6.1.6 (spec v1.28.0) — `approval` is a member of the closed set, so a rule carrying it must load. Guards against an SDK that closed the key set in v1.27.0 and never reopened it for the new field.
§6.1.6 rule 2 — `approval: required` on a `deny` rule is meaningless and MUST be rejected at load. Acting on half of a governance rule is the failure §6.1.5 exists to end.
